resolution: Closed by new CRIT-010 (contracts/sprint-1.md), independently re-verified in round-3's verdict.json: CRIT-010 now names and requires re-running driver-preconditions.test.mjs:81,89,96's PROP-015/PROP-016 tests by exact string, and control-flow-reads lib/driver.mjs:235-246 confirming both the akashKeyName and expectedBaseSignerAddress checks textually precede every lock/price/route/broadcast call. This finding is retained verbatim below for audit-trail purposes only and is NO LONGER a blocking finding as of round 3 (see reviews/contracts/sprint-1/output/verdict.json, blockingFindings: []).
description: The round-2 rewrite of CRIT-006 (which correctly fixes round-1's FIND-002 shared-env-fallback defect) entirely replaced CRIT-006's prior content with resolve-swap-identity.mjs/bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs-focused criteria, and in doing so silently DROPPED all contract coverage of a second, distinct REQ-009 money-safety mechanism: lib/driver.mjs's runSwap() own defense-in-depth identity-pin check at lines 239-244 (`if (deps.akashKeyName !== REQUIRED_AKASH_KEY_NAME) return {ok:false, status:'invalid_akash_key_name'}` and `const actualBaseSignerAddress = await deps.baseSigner.getAddress(); if (actualBaseSignerAddress !== deps.expectedBaseSignerAddress) return {ok:false, status:'unexpected_base_signer_address'}`), and its two dedicated Tier-1 REQUIRED proof obligations PROP-015 and PROP-016 (verification-architecture.md lines 79-80, both `Required: true`), exercised by lib/__tests__/driver-preconditions.test.mjs's named tests at lines 81 ('PROP-015: Base signer resolving to an unexpected/unpinned address -> non-zero exit, zero broadcast calls'), 89 ('PROP-016: AKASH_KEY_NAME unset -> non-zero exit, zero broadcast calls...'), and 96 ('PROP-016: AKASH_KEY_NAME set to a non-anicca-akash value -> non-zero exit, zero broadcast calls'). This is a REAL regression, not a pre-existing gap: round-1's verdict.json (edge_case_coverage dimension, PASS) explicitly cited the PRIOR version of CRIT-006 reading lib/driver.mjs:239-245's call-order and driver-preconditions.test.mjs:80-99's PROP-015/PROP-016 tests as its own evidence -- that coverage existed in round 1's contract and is now gone from round 2's contract entirely. Grepping contracts/sprint-1.md for 'PROP-015', 'PROP-016', and 'driver-preconditions' returns zero matches anywhere in the file. None of CRIT-001 through CRIT-009 directs the adversary to read lib/driver.mjs's runSwap() function (as opposed to its inner runInsideLock, which CRIT-001/CRIT-002 do name) or to re-run/inspect driver-preconditions.test.mjs by name. The ONLY mechanism that would catch a regression in this pin-check logic (e.g., an implementation that weakens the comparison to a substring/prefix match, drops the akashKeyName check, or removes the check entirely) is CRIT-008's blanket '98/98 passing' full-suite count -- exactly the class of insufficient scrutiny round-1's own FIND-001 established as blocking for PROP-019/PROP-023 ('never merely swept into CRIT-008's aggregate full-suite pass count... does not direct the adversary to independently confirm the SPECIFIC assertion strength'). A Phase-3 adversary following this contract verbatim (all 9 CRITs) could pass every criterion while never having read lib/driver.mjs's identity-pin preamble or driver-preconditions.test.mjs's PROP-015/PROP-016 tests at all -- the exact same failure mode round-1's FIND-001 was written to close, now reopened for a different REQ-009 proof obligation by the FIND-002 fix's side effect.

evidence.lineRange: 8-52 (CRIT-001..CRIT-009, no occurrence of 'PROP-015', 'PROP-016', or 'driver-preconditions' anywhere in the criteria block)
evidence.snippet: CRIT-006's passThreshold (lines 37) now cites only lib/__tests__/resolve-swap-identity.test.mjs and lib/__tests__/cli.test.mjs, and reads only bin/spawn-funding-swap.mjs's buildDeps() and lib/resolve-swap-identity.mjs -- it never cites lib/driver.mjs's runSwap() (lines 235-245) or lib/__tests__/driver-preconditions.test.mjs, where REQ-009's OTHER fail-closed mechanism (the pinned-address/akashKeyName comparison, PROP-015/PROP-016) actually lives.

fix: Add a dedicated CRIT (or restore a clause inside CRIT-006) whose passThreshold reads lib/driver.mjs's runSwap() lines 239-244 confirming the akashKeyName===REQUIRED_AKASH_KEY_NAME and actualBaseSignerAddress===deps.expectedBaseSignerAddress checks textually precede any lock/price/route/sign call, and names+re-runs driver-preconditions.test.mjs's PROP-015/PROP-016 tests by their exact names -- mirroring the exact-name-and-assertion-strength discipline CRIT-009 now correctly applies to PROP-019/PROP-023.
